Always confirm actual identifiers by inspecting the source code using get_code_snippet.

You will be given 9 opportunities to interact with functions to gather information for the debugging. An example diagnosis would look like follows.

Title: Diagnosis
Details: The corresponding issue report describes that tooltip text in the UI is displayed with HTML entities such as " instead of the intended characters. This strongly suggests a missing escaping or decoding step in tooltip generation. Inspecting the implementation of StandardToolTipTagFragmentGenerator.generateToolTipFragment reveals that it directly returns the toolTipText without applying any escaping. Recent issue reports mention similar encoding or escaping problems in related UI components, reinforcing the suspicion that this method lacks proper handling. The behavior observed in the code matches the issue report's symptoms, indicating that missing escaping in this method is the likely root cause.

After providing this diagnosis, you will be prompted to suggest which methods would be the best locations to be fixed. The answers should be in the form of `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` without commentary (one per line), as your answer will be automatically processed before finally being presented to the user.

messages.content:
" *

Checks if the CharSequence contains any character in the given * set of characters.

* *

A null CharSequence will return false. * A null or zero length search array will return false.

* * 
     * StringUtils.containsAny(null, *)                = false
     * StringUtils.containsAny("", *)                  = false
     * StringUtils.containsAny(*, null)                = false
     * StringUtils.containsAny(*, [])                  = false
     * StringUtils.containsAny("zzabyycdxx",['z','a']) = true
     * StringUtils.containsAny("zzabyycdxx",['b','y']) = true
     * StringUtils.containsAny("aba", ['z'])           = false
     *
* * @param cs the CharSequence to check, may be null * @param searchChars the chars to search for, may be null * @return the true if any of the chars are found, * false if no match or null input * @since 2.4 "

Title: Diagnosis
Details:
- Failing test: org.apache.commons.lang3.StringUtilsEqualsIndexOfTest.testContainsAnyCharArrayWithSupplementaryChars
  - It asserts: assertEquals(false, StringUtils.containsAny(CharU20000, CharU20001.toCharArray()))
  - Where CharU20000 = "\uD840\uDC00" (U+20000) and CharU20001 = "\uD840\uDC01" (U+20001).
  - Expected: false, because U+20000 ≠ U+20001.
- Bug report summary: StringUtils methods do not handle Unicode supplementary characters (Unicode 2.0+) correctly; containsAny matches incorrectly.
- Implementation inspected: StringUtils.containsAny(CharSequence cs, char[] searchChars)
  - Core loop (lines 1446–1453) iterates over each char of the input CharSequence and compares it to each char in the search array:
    - for each i: ch = cs.charAt(i)
    - for each j: if (searchChars[j] == ch) return true
  - There is no handling of surrogate pairs; it treats chars in isolation.
- How the failure occurs:
  - CharU20000 consists of two UTF-16 code units: [D840, DC00] (high surrogate, low surrogate).
  - CharU20001.toCharArray() yields [D840, DC01] (high surrogate, low surrogate).
  - The method compares single chars. On i = 0, ch = D840 (high surrogate). It finds a match at searchChars[0] == D840 and returns true immediately.
  - This is a false positive: matching just the high surrogate does not mean the supplementary code point matches; the low surrogate differs (DC00 vs DC01).
- Root cause:
  - containsAny(CharSequence, char[]) operates at the UTF-16 code unit (char) level and returns true upon matching any single char, which breaks for supplementary characters requiring surrogate pairs.
  - Proper handling should compare Unicode code points or, at minimum, detect surrogate pairs and require both high and low surrogates to match as a unit.
- Conclusion:
  - The method incorrectly returns true because it matches only the high surrogate of a supplementary character. It lacks logic to handle surrogate pairs/code points, causing the test to fail for U+20000 vs U+20001.

Your answer will be processed automatically, so make sure to only answer with the accurate signatures of all likely culprits (in `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` format), without commentary (one per line).
